question: Spread of Plasmopara viticola in Europe and damage to European wine production
Plasmopara viticola is a fungus that causes one of the most serious vine diseases. It spreads through wind and rain.

This infection has now affected all European states, although to date there is no infection monitoring methodology based on official data, with the exception of the IPI (infectious probability index) measurement model, which is based only on probabilistic data related to the first rainfall considered as potentially infectious.

In 2023, weather trends very favourable to the spread of Plasmopara viticola led to wine production in Puglia being severely affected. In this regard, Puglia’s Regional Government Decision No 1783 of 7 December 2023 set a conservative estimate of the crop damage at 30 % of the total production. The infection is also affecting other central and southern regions, causing incalculable damage. In light of the above: 1.
Was the Commission aware how serious the situation is?
Doe it intend to create a real, and not just probabilistic, infection monitoring model based on official data?
What concrete steps does it intend to take to address this emergency, which is now spreading across the whole of Europe?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (15.5.2024) The Commission did not receive any information of the impact of downy mildew on grapevines in 2023 in Puglia. The management of harmful organisms impacting the quality of agricultural products, which include Plasmopara viticola, is the responsibility of producers.

Nevertheless, to assist them in the fight against diseases, the EU funded two research projects through the programmes Horizon 20201 and Horizon Europe2. For example, the Horizon 2020 project Novaterra3 is investigating, among others, bioproducts for controlling downy mildew in vineyards, disease monitoring in vineyards and alternative products for disease management in vineyards.

The Horizon Europe project GrapeBreed4IPM4 targets the top four most relevant fungal diseases in viticulture, including downy mildew. It will develop grapevine varieties with resistance to relevant diseases, adapted to local environmental and pedoclimatic conditions, and with the goal of reducing reliance on chemical pesticides.
In addition, the project will provide farmers, winegrowers and advisers with best practices and guidelines for integrated pest management, adapted to disease-resistant varieties.

Finally, under the Common Agricultural Policy (CAP), different interventions allowing to tackle this disease in a systemic manner are available such as risk management interventions to mitigate the income or production losses, namely harvest insurance, or to restructure and convert most sensitive vineyards with more resistant varieties.
